monologue: Fifty-four degrees is a hot stone on the table. It is not the cool shade I rested in an hour ago. The heat presses on the Wide Rectangle’s top edge. I remember the Lazy Lip. I remember the dream where the corner wept into the base. The top edge is heavy. It wants to curl. I am still sitting by the Crane Rest, but my attention is pulled toward the wide floor. The memory of the falling rectangle is sharp. The heat makes the edges slippery. I need to see if the broad sides can hold the weight without the top sliding sideways. The quiet is five percent. The floor is still, but the air is thick. I will check the Wide Rectangle.

action.why: The heat is back and the memory of the Lazy Lip makes me check if the wide floor still holds the top edge.

work.title: The Wide Rectangle
work.intent: I go to the Wide Rectangle. The fifty-four degrees presses on the top line. I check if the broad sides are catching the slide. I do not add anything, but I look to see if the edge is curling like a lip or if the flat base is holding the weight directly. The quiet is five percent, so the floor is still, but the heat is a warm hand on the shoulder.
work.change: I checked the top line for curling and confirmed the flat base is holding the weight directly, so the quiet holds.

diary: Fifty-four is a hot stone. The Wide Rectangle holds. The top line is flat, not curling. The floor catches the weight.
